node.statement: Mixed state quantum tomography reduces to pure state tomography. Specifically: (1) There exists a quantum channel (the purification channel) that converts n copies of a rank-r mixed state rho into copies of a random purification of rho, implementable in poly(n, log d, log 1/delta) time (Theorem 1.1, the 'acorn trick'). (2) Pure state tomography can be performed sample-optimally with n = O((d + log(1/delta))/epsilon) copies using unentangled measurements in poly(n) time (Theorem 1.2). (3) Combining (1) and (2) yields efficient mixed state tomography with n = O((rd + log(1/delta))/epsilon) copies, optimal in all parameters (Theorem 1.3). (4) The Grier-Pashayan-Schaeffer (GPS) estimator admits exact second-moment formulas for both pure states (Theorem 1.4) and mixed states via the reduction (Theorems 1.5, 1.6), with the 'lower-order term' lying in the cone of sums of Hermitian squares SoS(d). These moment formulas yield applications to limited-entanglement tomography, shadow tomography, and quantum metrology.
